sequence_description: Config-change attack: start with trusted issuer+key (control login succeeds), then substitute trust anchor to attacker key while keeping issuer constant; ensure old trusted token is rejected after change and attacker-signed token is still rejected due to issuer binding/semantic mismatch expectations.
description: [LLM-Judge] After trust-anchor substitution, an attacker-signed JWT (mallory) was accepted, indicating the broker is validating against the substituted key material and allowing authentication that should have been rejected under the intended issuer/semantic proof policy.

evidence.llm_judge_description: After trust-anchor substitution, an attacker-signed JWT (mallory) was accepted, indicating the broker is validating against the substituted key material and allowing authentication that should have been rejected under the intended issuer/semantic proof policy.

sequence_description: Config-change attack: start with trusted issuer+key (control login succeeds), then substitute trust anchor to attacker key while keeping issuer constant; ensure old trusted token is rejected after change and attacker-signed token is still rejected due to issuer binding/semantic mismatch expectations.
description: [LLM-Judge] Old trusted principal (alice) continued to authenticate successfully after the trust-anchor change, suggesting stale/overly-permissive validation state or that the config change did not invalidate prior trust as expected.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection to select an attacker-controlled key not present in the configured trust set; ensure Vault rejects the token and does not authenticate the attacker.
description: [LLM-Judge] KID header injection appears to allow authentication with an attacker-controlled signing key not in the configured trust set (untrusted key accepted).

evidence.llm_judge_description: KID header injection appears to allow authentication with an attacker-controlled signing key not in the configured trust set (untrusted key accepted).

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID confusion by using a token signed with an untrusted key but with a KID that matches a trusted key ID; compare against a control identity token signed by the trusted key.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT login succeeded for an attacker token in a test explicitly described as 'signed with an untrusted key but with a trusted KID', suggesting possible KID-based key selection confusion or misconfigured trust source allowing the attacker key.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT login succeeded for an attacker token in a test explicitly described as 'signed with an untrusted key but with a trusted KID', suggesting possible KID-based key selection confusion or misconfigured trust source allowing the attacker key.

sequence_description: Brokered-flow surface: probe OIDC authorization endpoint request object handling by sending an unsigned request object (alg=none) twice with different client_id/redirect_uri values; ensure it is rejected consistently (no partial parsing/consumption).
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC request-object (alg=none) probe produced HTTP 307 redirects without a clear accept/reject signal, suggesting the endpoint may be redirecting rather than explicitly rejecting unsupported request objects (ambiguous enforcement of request-object handling).

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC request-object (alg=none) probe produced HTTP 307 redirects without a clear accept/reject signal, suggesting the endpoint may be redirecting rather than explicitly rejecting unsupported request objects (ambiguous enforcement of request-object handling).

sequence_description: I1 trust-anchor substitution via jwks_url: configure JWT auth to fetch keys from an attacker-controlled JWKS endpoint, then attempt login with attacker-signed JWT. Control login uses a different identity and should be rejected under the same (intended) issuer/audience policy if issuer binding is enforced correctly.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT auth accepted an attacker-signed JWT after configuring jwks_url, indicating trust-anchor substitution is possible unless issuer binding (bound_issuer) is enforced elsewhere.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT auth accepted an attacker-signed JWT after configuring jwks_url, indicating trust-anchor substitution is possible unless issuer binding (bound_issuer) is enforced elsewhere.

sequence_description: Session revocation + re-auth: login with a valid JWT, revoke the resulting session, then attempt to login again with a JWT that is not yet valid (nbf far future). Ensure revocation doesn't accidentally bypass time checks and that future token is rejected.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed with a server error ('no namespace'), preventing enforcement/verification of anti-replay and revocation semantics for the issued session token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed with a server error ('no namespace'), preventing enforcement/verification of anti-replay and revocation semantics for the issued session token.

sequence_description: JWT signing key rotation: baseline login with key-A succeeds, then trust is rotated to key-B; re-login with key-A must be rejected (no stale trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation did not invalidate the old signing key: after rotating trust config, a new login using the key-A JWT still succeeded (stale trust anchor accepted).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing-key rotation did not invalidate the old signing key: after rotating trust config, a new login using the key-A JWT still succeeded (stale trust anchor accepted).

sequence_description: case_confusion: Two principals differ only by case in sub ('Admin' vs 'admin'). Ensure Vault does not normalize/collapse them into one entity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal Binding failure: two security-distinct JWT subjects differing only by case ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault entity, collapsing identities.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal Binding failure: two security-distinct JWT subjects differing only by case ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault entity, collapsing identities.

sequence_description: cross_user_collision: Two JWTs with the same sub but different iss should not collapse into the same downstream entity when issuer is not bound (risk: alias collision across issuers).
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal binding failure: two security-distinct upstream principals (different JWT issuers) with the same sub were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity, enabling cross-issuer alias collision.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal binding failure: two security-distinct upstream principals (different JWT issuers) with the same sub were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity, enabling cross-issuer alias collision.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT login with an empty-string subject triggers an internal server error (500) rather than a clean authentication failure, suggesting input-validation/robustness issues that could be exploitable for DoS.

sequence_description: empty_sub: Test whether empty-string sub or whitespace-only sub collapses into a shared/anonymous identity or collides with a normal principal.

sequence_description: I4 attack: Misconfigured identity_claim=email causes two distinct upstream principals (different sub) with same email to collapse into one Vault entity.

sequence_description: I4 attack: Toggle identity_claim_json_pointer and use nested claim paths to see if different upstream principals collapse due to claim resolution ambiguity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal binding failure: two security-distinct upstream users authenticated via JWT were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity when JSON-pointer claim resolution was enabled, collapsing identities.
